author: ABC7Chicago
title: Chicago weather: Strong storms knock down trees, power lines in parts of area
text:
Severe storms moved through the Chicago area Wednesday evening, leaving behind damage in some places.
The storm ripped through East Dundee around 6:30 p.m. There was a tornado warning at that time, but neighbors ABC7 talked to say they believed it was just really strong wind, but they saw no rotation.
Either way, it was enough to knock down several large trees and power lines. The storms came quickly through the northwest suburbs causing damage in a path from Algonquin to Streamwood. Downed trees in Streamwood mangled cars and smashed windows. And in Bartlett, which got hit hard by a tornado a little over a week ago, got hit again Wednesday night.
While the majority of damage appears to have been in the northwest suburbs, storms also caused damage in the south side of the city in the Beverly neighborhood. An Algonquin resident captured video of what appeared to be rotation from a cell phone. That storm mostly caused tree damage. The Storm Prediction Center had the city of Chicago, most suburbs and Northwest Indiana under a Level 2 risk for severe weather Wednesday.
There is a Level 1 risk for areas to the areas far west and south of the Chicago area. Thunderstorms that developed in southwest Wisconsin were on track to enter the Chicago area during the afternoon and early evening hours, ABC7 AccuWeather meteorologists said.
